newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bolger's view of NZ National's chances unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bolger's view of NZ National's chances unchanged.

text.p: Caretaker Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Thursday he rated his National Party's chances of swinging a coalition deal with the New Zealand First Party as 50:50.
He was speaking after a three hour 50 minute meeting with NZ First, the longest so far in talks which have dragged on for six weeks since the inconclusive October 12 election.
Asked if the talks were swinging National's way, he said: "I'm still saying it's 50:50."
Asked why the talks took so long, Bolger said: "Well we are doing a lot of work obviously."
He declined to give any details about the talks.

Asked about when he thought a decision would be made, he said: "Parliament has to open in the week starting December 10, it doesn't have to...I guess that's a pretty easily defined deadline...and I'm sure everybody would like to have this finalised before then."
